text: A thermopile is astonishingly sensitive. It can register the warmth of a person standing a few metres away, or of the Moon. It is used to measure radiant heat, in radiation pyrometers for furnaces, in infrared detectors and burglar alarms. Run the Peltier way, the same kind of device makes portable coolers. And thermoelectric generators, heated by plutonium, power deep space probes like Voyager.
